text:
Maria Chen: proposing a small RFC for a unified fallback routing policy. idea: prefer in-pod sidecar gRPC to the model pool, fallback to gateway-transcoded REST only when sidecar cannot satisfy (e.g., model not pinned, capacity). need to think quotas + telemetry + rollout UX. thoughts?

Akshay Patel: +1 to prefer gRPC sidecar for perf. main worry is strict quota enforcement if we let sidecars short-circuit the gateway. how do we bind per-tenant quotas when requests bypass central gateway?

Jordan Rivera: we should measure fallback-rate as a core signal in the console. dashboard panels: fallback-rate (per minute, per-tenant), P50/P95 latency for gRPC vs fallback, quota-violation events, and successful fallback fallthroughs. tags: region, tenant_id, model_variant, route_policy.

Sophia Li: rollout UX: we can expose a canary toggle per-tenant that forces fallback path so we can validate gateway behavior. also need opt-in for tenants who want enforced global quotas (enterprise).

Lin Park: technically, implement in two parts: (1) sidecar routing decision + optimistic call to local inference. if sidecar detects quota-exempt or local capacity unreachable -> annotate and forward to gateway with X-Redwood-Fallback: reason. (2) gateway enforces final quota accounting and metrics. small envoy config snippet we used in spike: 
```
- name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
    request_headers_to_add:
      - header: { key: "x-fallback-reason", value: "%DOWNSTREAM_REASON%" }
```

Akshay Patel: that helps. but for proto vs JSON: if sidecars expose gRPC+proto internally we get type safety and cheaper payloads. gateway can do transcoding for external REST clients. caveat: streaming RPCs are tricky to transcode. we likely need to disallow streaming on the public REST surface or implement a websocket bridge.

Maria Chen: agreed. recommendation: internal-only gRPC/protobuf for route-to-runtime, gateway as optional HTTP transcoder for public API. internal request attributes to include: priority_hint, latency_sla_ms, cost_tier. example proto snippet: 
```
message InferenceRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string model = 2;
  bytes prompt = 3;
  map<string,string> attributes = 4; // priority_hint, latency_sla_ms
}
```

Jordan Rivera: for dashboards we should derive synthetic metrics: fallback_latency_delta = fallback_p95 - grpc_p95; fallback_cost_ratio; quota_enforcement_gap = gateway_enforced_count - sidecar_enforced_count. chart those over time. add alert: fallback_rate > 5% for > 5m in prod.

Sophia Li: UX question: if tenant opts into "strict gateway quotas" do we route all requests through gateway even when sidecar could handle? that's probably OK for enterprise but will add latency. need clear checkbox in tenant settings and an estimated cost/latency tradeoff warning.

Lin Park: can do tenant policy: route_override: ["force_gateway", "prefer_sidecar"]. default prefer_sidecar. Implement via service discovery flag that sidecar checks on init + periodic refresh. small pseudo-code: 
```
if (tenant.policy == FORCE_GATEWAY) { forwardToGateway(req) }
else { tryLocalOrForward(req) }
```

Maria Chen: outstanding questions: 1) whether quota accounting needs synchronous enforcement at gateway (i.e., fail fast) vs async reconciliation; 2) how we tag traces so traces that span sidecar->gateway show fallback_reason; 3) rollout plan that minimizes blast radius.

Akshay Patel: 1) enterprise quotas probably need sync enforcement at gateway to guarantee limits. for self-serve, async reconciliation with throttles is ok. 2) add trace span attribute fallback_reason and route_policy. 3) rollout: feature flag gated, start with internal tenants, then 5% of traffic across low-risk tenants, then 25%, etc. use canary signals: error rate, fallback-rate, quota-failures, cost variance.

Dev Platform: deploy-bot ran a dry-run for the envoy snippet in staging, no regressions. ops-bot recorded metric: staging fallback_rate 0.8% during the test window. planning a small canary tomorrow at 08:30 PT if we agree on heuristics.

Sophia Li: sounds good. next steps: Maria draft short RFC with config schema, metric names, tenant policy options, and rollout checklist. I'll own dashboard panels. Lin will prototype sidecar flag + header propagation. Akshay will write quota enforcement options. Jordan will sketch alert rules.

Maria Chen: I'll open the RFC PR this afternoon. tagging @Dev Platform for infra review and @ops-bot for monitoring playbook. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
